关键词: Trade Facilitation and Trade Enforcement Act of 2015
主要内容: On April 29, 2016, the U.S. Department of the Treasury released a report on the foreign exchange policies of major trading partners of the United States. The report implements the provisions of the Trade Facilitation and Trade Enforcement Act of 2015, which provides new tools for monitoring and addressing unfair currency practices. The report highlights that the U.S. economy grew at a solid pace of 2.4 percent in 2015, while growth in other advanced economies was more disappointing. Emerging market economies are facing significant headwinds from low commodity prices, weak trade growth, and internal cyclical dynamics. Based on the new tools provided under the Act, the report establishes a new 'Monitoring List' which finds that five major trading partners of the United States – China, Japan, Korea, Taiwan, and Germany – met two of the three criteria for enhanced analysis. No economy currently meets all three criteria. The report notes that China has both a significant bilateral trade surplus with the United States and a material current account surplus. China has intervened heavily in the foreign exchange markets in recent months to support the RMB, after strong downward market pressure triggered by a surprise change in China’s foreign exchange policy last August. The report also points to Japan’s significant bilateral trade surplus with the United States and material current account surplus. Japan has not intervened in the foreign exchange market in over four years. Treasury assesses that current conditions in the dollar-yen foreign exchange market are orderly. Korea has a significant bilateral trade surplus with the United States and a material current account surplus. Treasury estimates that during the second half of 2015 through March 2016, the Korean authorities intervened to resist depreciation of the won during periods of financial market turbulence. The report urges Korea to limit its foreign exchange intervention only to circumstances of disorderly market conditions and to increase the transparency of its foreign exchange operations. Taiwan has a material current account surplus and, per Treasury estimates, has engaged in persistent net foreign currency purchases through most of 2015. The report calls on the authorities to limit foreign exchange interventions to the exceptional circumstances of disorderly market conditions, as well as increase the transparency of reserve holdings and foreign exchange market interventions. Germany has a significant bilateral trade surplus with the United States and a material current account surplus, which is the second largest globally. This surplus represents more than 8 percent of GDP and could support domestic demand. The Treasury stated that no major trading partner met the criteria for currency manipulation under Section 3004 of the Act during the report period. The report emphasized the importance of adhering to G-7, G-20, and IMF exchange rate commitments, including not targeting exchange rates and using all policy tools to boost demand. G-20 Finance Ministers and Central Bank Governors endorsed this view in February and April 2016.
